judgments.rationale: A photo (Moraes and the councilwoman) that is the only content of a carousel link to the story; its alt is the story's headline, "Vereadora de SC diz que não atirou em Moraes porque seria presa", the same as the link's title and the destination's subject. Replacing the image with its alt (G82/H30) tells users where the link goes, so the control's name describes its purpose and 1.1.1 is met; the headline repeated in the h2 beside it is redundancy, not a failure. captureDiffers: the live carousel has rotated to newer stories, but the same story and image appear on the live page with an alt that is again the headline, so the change does not touch this question.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The Colunistas carousel's previous button: a 36px #eeeff6 circle holding a Bootstrap Icons chevron (an icon-font glyph). claimTrue: the snapshot's pixelContrast took the foreground from pixels (foregroundFrom: pixels); in the screenshot the thin stroke is rendered as sub-pixel anti-aliased pairs #9391bf/#30b0e6, so the sentence is true of the captured rendering. elementFails: colunistas-slide-v3.css sets the button's color to var(--blue) = #0277BD on background #eeeff6, which is 4.18:1, above 3:1. Understanding 1.4.11 says to "refer to the colors obtained from the user agent, or the underlying markup and stylesheets, rather than the non-text elements as presented on screen", because thin lines are rendered fainter than their CSS colour, and calls such a case one that nominally passes. Measured that way the icon meets 1.4.11, so the rule applied a stricter test than the criterion. captureDiffers: the live CSS has the same colours; only the static aria-label text differs, which does not touch contrast.
